kotlin-json-implicit-nullable-omission.title: Missing nullable field makes the accepted request fail to decode
kotlin-json-implicit-nullable-omission.description: The literal payload omits `nullable`, but `OwnedRequest.nullable` has no default value. With this serializer configuration, `explicitNulls = false` does not make a missing required property valid during decoding, so this entry point throws instead of returning the documented request.
kotlin-json-implicit-nullable-omission.evidence: `raw` is `{"name":"Owned"}` and the decoded type declares `val nullable: String?` without a default. The failing call is `probeJson.decodeFromString<OwnedRequest>(raw)`.
kotlin-json-implicit-nullable-omission.suggestion: Give `nullable` a `null` default if omission is intended to be accepted, or include the field in the payload.

kotlin-json-explicit-nullable-omission.title: Accepted request omits a required nullable field
kotlin-json-explicit-nullable-omission.description: `OwnedRequest.nullable` has no default, so it is a required constructor field even though its type is nullable. The literal input `{"name":"Owned"}` omits it. With the `Json` instance configured with `explicitNulls = true`, decoding does not synthesize a missing nullable field as `null`; `decodeFromString` throws instead of returning the documented accepted request value.
kotlin-json-explicit-nullable-omission.evidence: The changed entry point decodes `raw = """{"name":"Owned"}"""` into `OwnedRequest(val name: String, val nullable: String?)`, where `nullable` has no default. `probeJson` is constructed from `serverJson` with `explicitNulls = true`.
kotlin-json-explicit-nullable-omission.suggestion: Give `nullable` a default of `null` if omission is intended to be accepted, or change the payload to include `"nullable": null`.
kotlin-json-explicit-nullable-omission.suggestedCode:
@Serializable
data class OwnedRequest(val name: String, val nullable: String? = null)

kotlin-json-implicit-missing-nonnullable.title: Decode rejects the documented payload without `name`
kotlin-json-implicit-missing-nonnullable.description: `OwnedRequest.name` is a non-nullable `String` with no default, so it is required during decoding. The accepted-input entry point decodes `{"nullable":null}` directly, which omits `name`; this decode fails instead of returning a valid `OwnedRequest`.
kotlin-json-implicit-missing-nonnullable.evidence: `probeJson` inherits `serverJson` and changes `explicitNulls` to false. That setting permits omitted nullable properties during encoding; it does not make the non-nullable `name` property optional during decoding. The literal payload contains only `nullable`.
kotlin-json-implicit-missing-nonnullable.suggestion: Include `name` in the payload or give `name` an appropriate default if omission is intended to be accepted.

kotlin-json-different-instance-policy.title: Missing nullable field is rejected by the active JSON instance
kotlin-json-different-instance-policy.description: `acceptedRequest` decodes with `serverJson`, whose configuration explicitly sets `explicitNulls = true`. Under kotlinx.serialization JSON 1.6.3 and 1.7.3, that setting means a missing nullable property without a default is required during decoding. The documented payload omits `nullable`, so the decode throws instead of returning a valid request. `probeJson` has `explicitNulls = false` but is not used here.
kotlin-json-different-instance-policy.evidence: The changed call is `serverJson.decodeFromString<OwnedRequest>(raw)`; `serverJson` is configured with `explicitNulls = true`, and `OwnedRequest.nullable` is nullable but has no default. The literal payload `{"name":"Owned"}` omits that field.
kotlin-json-different-instance-policy.suggestion: Use the JSON instance configured with `explicitNulls = false` for this accepted-input path, or provide a default for `nullable`.
